Tail state keyed by a **stable identifier** (e.g. `log.txt`) rather than the absolute path, so a container migration preserves the offset — done in `fa09b10ee`

Offset advances **per successful batch**, not only after the final one, so a flaky link makes forward progress and already-uploaded batches are not re-sent — done in `a892be0ff`, by the equivalent route: each pass reads at most `maxEventsPerRequest` lines and therefore yields exactly one batch, which collapses "advance after all batches" and "advance per batch" into the same thing. Progress is banked under any transient failure.

A missing offset for an already-large file seeds to **EOF**, not 0 — a fresh install or migration must not attempt to backfill the entire log history — done in `fa09b10ee`, `seedToEndOfFileThreshold = 1 MiB`. Files under the threshold still start at 0, since they upload in full in one pass.

Existing `log_prev.txt` stall drains or is abandoned deliberately rather than retried forever — **abandoned deliberately.** `fa09b10ee` applies the same seed-to-EOF rule to `pair.previousPath`, so the stalled ~12 MB `log_prev.txt` is seeded to its own size and never re-queued. The lines already lost to the 2026-08-16 outage stay lost; the alternative was retrying a 170-POST pass forever.
